verses.gurmukhi: ਲੋਚਨ ਸ੍ਰਵਨ ਮੁਖ ਨਾਸਿਕਾ ਹਸਤ ਪਗ ਚਿਹਨ ਅਨੇਕ ਮਨ ਮੇਕ ਜੈਸੇ ਜਾਨੀਐ ॥
verses.translit_en: lochan sravan mukh naasikaa hasat pag chihan anek man mek jaise jaaneeaai ||

en.bdb: As the mind is associated with eyes, ears, mouth, nose, hand, feet etc., and other limbs of the body; it is the driving force behind them:

verses.gurmukhi: ਅੰਗ ਅੰਗ ਪੁਸ਼ਟ ਤੁਸ਼ਟਮਾਨ ਹੋਤ ਜੈਸੇ ਏਕ ਮੁਖ ਸ੍ਵਾਦ ਰਸ ਅਰਪਤਿ ਮਾਨੀਐ ॥
verses.translit_en: a(n)g a(n)g pushaT tushaTamaan hot jaise ek mukh savaiaadh ras arapat maaneeaai ||

en.bdb: As tasty and wholesome food is eaten by the mouth that makes every limb of the body strong, and blooming;

verses.gurmukhi: ਮੂਲ ਏਕ ਸਾਖਾ ਪਰ ਸਾਖਾ ਜਲ ਜਿਉ ਅਨੇਕ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਬਿਬੇਕ ਜਾਵਦੇਕ ਉਰ ਆਨੀਐ ॥
verses.translit_en: mool ek saakhaa par saakhaa jal jiau anek braham bibek jaavadhek ur aaneeaai ||

en.bdb: As watering the trunk of a tree conveys water to its many big or small branches. So far as the question of the universe arises, one should bring to mind the thought of one Lord who is all-pervading.

verses.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਦਰਪਨ ਦੇਖੀਆਤ ਆਪਾ ਆਪੁ ਆਤਮ ਅਵੇਸ ਪਰਮਾਤਮ ਗਿਆਨੀਐ ॥੨੪੫॥
verses.translit_en: gurmukh dharapan dhekheeaat aapaa aap aatam aves paramaatam giaaneeaai ||245||

en.bdb: As one sees self in the mirror, so does an obedient disciple of the Guru focuses his mind in his self (a miniscule part of the Lord-soul) and recognises the all-pervading Lord. (245)
